body:
## Problem

`pdca cleanup` closes every COMPLETE close/no-fix bundle's issue at once, as **not planned** (`template/src/pdca_harness/cleanup.py:425-432` on `main` @ `b5f5c29`). A `duplicate` close often has a condition attached, and cleanup can't see it:

- **#624** (bundle issue_624, close disposition `duplicate`). Its brief says: comment on #624 now, and close it only when #652's PR merges, through `Fixes #624` in that PR's body (`results/issue_624/brief.md:19`, `:33`). Cleanup would close it today as "not planned", before the fix exists. If #652 is later descoped, #624's gap is lost.
- **#630** (bundle issue_630, close disposition `duplicate` of #463). Its brief leaves it to the human to choose: close it, or keep it open as the bug that blocks #463 (`results/issue_630/brief.md:15`, criteria b and c). Cleanup would close it no matter which.

"Not planned" is also the wrong reason for a duplicate. GitHub has a `duplicate` close reason, and the comment should name the issue it duplicates.

Neither bundle records its target or condition in a form the driver can read, so cleanup has nothing to check.

## Done when

A close bundle can record a machine-readable "duplicate of #N" and an optional "close when <PR/issue> is merged/closed" condition. `pdca cleanup` then:
- closes it with reason `duplicate` and a comment naming #N,
- leaves it open (report only) while the condition is unmet,
- and when no condition is recorded for a `duplicate`, reports it and does not close it.

A test pins each of the three.

Found by the eduralph/pdca-pdca Act review of 2026-10-10 (bundles issue_624 and issue_630).
title: cleanup: a `duplicate` close bundle is closed at once as "not planned" — no "duplicate of #N", no "close when PR X merges" condition
